subject: History
description: Slave, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi dynasties

questions.stem: The founder of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was:
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a slave-general of Muhammad Ghori, became the first Sultan of Delhi in 1206 after Ghori's death — founding the Slave or Mamluk dynasty. He began the Qutub Minar (completed by Iltutmish) and the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque. Iltutmish (1211-36) was Aibak's son-in-law and successor; Balban (1266-87) consolidated the dynasty's power.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Market-control regulations and price-fixing in Delhi's bazaars were famously introduced by:
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316) introduced sweeping market reforms — fixed prices for grain, cloth, horses and slaves; set up three separate markets under a Diwan-i-Riyasat; maintained buffer stocks. He did this mainly to pay a standing army cheaply. He also imposed a tax on produce (kharaj) at half the yield and a house tax (ghari).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Tughlaq sultan who shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and issued token currency was:
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-51) tried to move the capital from Delhi to Devagiri (renamed Daulatabad) in 1327, forcing an unpopular mass migration, and issued copper/brass token coins that counterfeiters promptly forged, causing economic chaos. Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, visited his court. Ghiyas-ud-din founded the dynasty; Firoz Shah (1351-88) was his cousin and successor.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The only woman sultan of Delhi was:
questions.explanation: Razia Sultana (r. 1236-40), daughter of Iltutmish, was the only woman to sit on the throne of Delhi. She was overthrown by the Turkish nobility (the 'Forty' / Chahalgani) after a short reign. Nur Jahan was Jahangir's wife (Mughal, not Sultanate); Chand Bibi defended Ahmednagar against Akbar; Mumtaz Mahal was Shah Jahan's queen (the Taj's namesake).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, defeated by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat (1526), was:
questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi (1517-26) was the last sultan of Delhi. Babur defeated and killed him at Panipat on 21 April 1526, using cannons and the 'tulughma' flanking tactic; the Mughal empire began. Bahlol (1451-89) founded the Lodi line; Sikandar (1489-1517) moved the capital to Agra and was Ibrahim's father. Daulat Khan Lodi, governor of Punjab, actually invited Babur to invade.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The founder of the Khilji dynasty of Delhi was:
questions.explanation: Jalal-ud-din Firuz Khilji (1290-96) founded the dynasty by overthrowing the Slave dynasty's last ruler. He was assassinated in 1296 by his nephew and son-in-law Ali Gurshasp, who became Alauddin Khilji. The dynasty ended in 1320 with the usurpation by Khusraw Khan and the rise of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Qutub Minar in Delhi was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and later completed by:
questions.explanation: Aibak started the minaret c. 1192; after his death only the first storey was complete. Iltutmish (1211-36) added three more storeys. In 1368 Firoz Shah Tughlaq repaired damage from a lightning strike and added the fifth storey. Alauddin Khilji built the Alai Darwaza (1311) next to the minar but not the minar itself.
